exercise.name: Lever Standing Single Leg Calf Raise

reference.title: Lever Standing Single Leg Calf Raise
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the heel rises, inhale as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and light: balance limits it before the calf does. Pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Heavier bar, then the ball of the foot on a low step for a deeper range

cues.text: Step under the shoulder yoke of the calf machine, hands on its handles, and stand up straight to lift the lever. Stand on the right foot, left foot lifted behind with the knee bent, body tall.
Breathe out and rise as high as you can onto the ball of the right foot.
Pause at the top; stand tall, ankle straight, weight over the big toe.
Breathe in and lower the heel slowly to the floor; the lever comes down with you.
Touch down lightly and repeat; then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Losing balance with a heavy bar
mistakes.fix: Go lighter, stand inside a rack with the safeties set, or hold a support with one hand and use dumbbells instead.
Keep the pressure through the big and second toes.
Knee straight but soft; slow lowering, pause at the top.
Squeeze the glutes and keep the pelvis level over the standing foot.

kinematics.norm: Full range to as high as possible (clinical opinion); the heel-rise test counts only full-height rises (Hébert-Losier 2017)
As high as possible each rep (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Standing knee ≈4°, free knee ≈80° (foot lifted behind)
kinematics.norm: Straight but not locked (clinical opinion); knee angle did not change triceps surae fatigue in single-leg heel raises at 0 vs 45 degrees (Hébert-Losier 2012)

kinematics.setup: High bar on the upper traps, 80 cm grip (handle centres); body + bar centre of mass 5 cm ahead of the ankle
kinematics.peak: Centre of mass 1.5 cm behind the ball of the foot at the top (pelvis shifted 10.9 cm over the standing foot)
kinematics.norm: Shoulder yoke across the upper back, hands on its handles just outside the shoulders (machine design)

kinematics.peak: 1.0 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down, 0.6 s reset
kinematics.norm: About 1 s up, a short pause, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Lift the lever off its stop with both feet on the floor before shifting onto one leg; put it back the same way.
Start light: balance on one leg under the yoke is the hard part; stop the set if you wobble.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance trouble: hold a dumbbell in one hand and steady yourself on a wall or rack with the other.
Achilles pain: smaller range and lighter load, slow tempo.
regressions: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise with a hand on the wall.
progressions: Ball of the foot on a low step for a deeper stretch.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Whole triceps surae with the knee straight; one leg carries the body weight plus the bar. Standing (knee straight) training grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated training (Kinoshita 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk tall and stiff under the bar (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back upright under the bar (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back upright under the bar (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the free knee bent behind (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The shelf the bar rests on (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The shelf the bar rests on (clinical opinion).
